lines: @@ -56,6 +56,7 @@ Configuration is via CLI flags (`--help` for the full list):

- `--listener-channel-error <seconds>` — `<seconds>` after its welcome, end every listener with the `channelError` (`Internal error`) and `disconnect` the API sends when a listener fails. The welcome is whichever event the listener opens with: `welcome`, or `welcomeback` / `reset` for a listener resuming from a `Last-Event-ID`. `0` sends them instead of the welcome, as when the API cannot set a listener up
- `--withhold-welcome` — keep listen requests open without ever welcoming them, as when the API hangs while setting a listener up. Mutually exclusive with `--listener-channel-error`

- `--withhold-welcome-probability <0..1>` — like `--withhold-welcome`, but each listen request is left unwelcomed at this probability while the rest work normally, e.g. `--withhold-welcome-probability 0.5`. Mutually exclusive with `--withhold-welcome` and `--listener-channel-error`

+  - `--refuse-listener <dataset-not-found|evicted>[:<seconds>]` — refuse every listener the way the API refuses one it will not serve. Unlike the flags above, reconnecting does not help, so this exercises how the studio handles a listener that fails irrecoverably. `dataset-not-found` replaces the welcome with the `channelError` (`namespaceNotFoundError`) and `disconnect` the API sends for a dataset that does not exist; `evicted` welcomes the listener, then sends the `disconnect` (`forced by provider`) the API sends a listener it has evicted. Append `:<seconds>` to let listeners work for that long after the proxy starts, so the studio boots and loads live first: at the deadline, every open listener is refused there and then (with the same events, mid-stream), and every listener opened later is refused at its welcome. Mutually exclusive with `--listener-channel-error`, `--withhold-welcome` and `--withhold-welcome-probability`, e.g. `pnpm dev:proxy --refuse-listener evicted` or `pnpm dev:proxy --refuse-listener dataset-not-found:60`
+        error: message`Expected "dataset-not-found" or "evicted", optionally followed by ":<seconds>" (a whole number), got ${input}.`,
+    return {success: true, value: {refusal: known, afterMs: afterSec * 1000}}
